channel.title: California Uzbek — Latest
channel.description: Independent analysis · Central Asia & world geopolitics

item.title: The Basmachi movement and the exodus (1918–1934): Turkestan's resistance and the flight to Afghanistan
item.description: The Basmachi were an armed movement that fought Soviet rule across Turkestan and Bukhara from 1918 into the early 1930s. Their defeat drove tens of thousands of fighters and civilians across the Amu Darya into Afghanistan, forming Central Asian émigré communities. This history explainer sets out the movement and the migration it caused on the basis of sources, with contested figures clearly flagged.

item.title: Tashkent to renovate 400 mahallas by 2030 under the ‘15-minute city’ principle
item.description: Tashkent will modernise 400 neighbourhood (mahalla) complexes by 2030 under the ‘15-minute mahalla’ principle, with 100 renovated by 2027. The whole programme is expected to create about 130,000 jobs. The plan was reviewed at a meeting chaired by the President on 14 October.

item.title: Uzbekistan recalculates unjustified utility debts for nearly 800,000 citizens
item.description: Following an inspection by the Competition Committee, 22 billion soums (about $1.8 million) in unjustified utility debts were recalculated in favour of citizens, restoring the rights of nearly 800,000 people. The main cause was that subscriber databases had not been updated.

item.title: How compound interest works and how your savings grow: simple vs compound interest, and the Rule of 72
item.description: Compound interest means interest added on top of interest — "interest on interest." It makes savings grow faster over time, but the same rule works against you on debt. This explainer covers the difference between simple and compound interest, the formula, the Rule of 72 and concrete examples, on the basis of sources. This is not financial advice.

item.title: Tashkent couriers and moped riders under police scrutiny: bikes being impounded
item.description: Tashkent traffic police have escalated checks on moped, scooter and e-bike riders, especially couriers. Registration has been required since October 2025 and an A1 licence since January 2026. According to Yandex, couriers have been fined more than 4.7 billion soums since the start of the year.

item.title: Uzbekistan launches a nationwide business census from 15 October
item.description: Under Government Resolution No. 557, a nationwide business census runs from 15 October to 30 November 2026. It covers all legal entities, entrepreneurs and informal businesses; results will be published by 1 September 2027. The unobserved economy is estimated at about 246 trillion soums (23%).

item.title: How cryptocurrency and blockchain work: the basics, Bitcoin and the risks
item.description: A cryptocurrency is a digital asset that works without a central bank or intermediary, using a distributed-ledger technology called blockchain. This explainer sets out, on the basis of sources only, how cryptocurrency and blockchain work, Bitcoin's history, mining, wallets and keys, stablecoins and the main risks. This is not financial advice.

item.title: Houthi attacks put Pakistan in a tough choice between Saudi Arabia and Iran
item.description: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia are testing Pakistan's ability to keep its security partnership with Riyadh while preserving ties with neighbouring Iran. Analysts warn Islamabad's military involvement could sharpen tensions with Tehran.

item.title: Uzbekistan signs law protecting children from violence: life imprisonment for rape
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev on 14 October signed a law strengthening protection of children from violence. Sexual offences against children under 14 now carry 15–25 years or life imprisonment, the statute of limitations is abolished, and child victims and witnesses are guaranteed state-funded lawyers.

item.title: How unemployment insurance works in the US: eligibility, amount, duration and the basics for immigrants
item.description: Unemployment insurance is a federal-state insurance system that pays temporary cash benefits to workers who lose their jobs through no fault of their own. It is funded by employer taxes and each state runs its own program. This explainer covers the structure of the system, eligibility, benefit amount and duration, and key points for immigrants — on the basis of sources.

item.title: The Uzbek diaspora in Japan: from the first workers of the 1970s to today's community of students and trainees
item.description: The Uzbek community in Japan is small but one of the country's fastest-growing diasporas: from 184 people in 2000 to 7,362 by the end of 2025. This historical explainer sets out the community's Soviet-era roots, its growth after independence, its main cities and the labor-migration agreements concluded with Japan — on the basis of sources, with precise dates and figures.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes 1 million soums in winter aid for low-income families
item.description: Under a draft by the National Agency for Social Protection, low-income families would receive a one-time 1 million soums in November 2026; the electricity allowance in non-gasified areas would rise to 350 kWh and compensation for liquefied gas would be introduced. The measures are proposed as part of energy-tariff reforms.

item.title: Mirziyoyev unveils an economic philosophy called “O‘Z”: “Capital has no nationality”
item.description: At a 12 October meeting with entrepreneurs and investors in New Tashkent, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev called for an end to distinguishing between foreign and domestic investors and presented the “O‘Z” philosophy (Uzbekistan, change, identity, responsibility).

item.title: What halal certification is and how to verify halal food in the US: marks, agencies and zabiha
item.description: In the United States halal food is certified not by the government but by private, independent certification bodies. This explainer sets out the concepts of halal and zabiha, the main US certifiers (IFANCA, ISA, AHF, HMS), how to check that a product is genuinely halal, and the halal system introduced in Uzbekistan — as sourced facts only.

item.title: Uzbekistan plans to restore monuments linked to Uzbek scholars in Afghanistan
item.description: A delegation of Uzbekistan's Agency of Cultural Heritage studied historical sites linked to Uzbek scholars and thinkers in four Afghan provinces — Balkh, Takhar, Sar-e Pul and Faryab. A cooperation memorandum with Afghanistan's Ministry of Information and Culture is planned.

item.title: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio to visit Samarkand with 200+ companies
item.description: Marco Rubio will take part in a C5+1 ministerial meeting with the foreign ministers of the five Central Asian states in Samarkand on 17–22 October 2026. According to the U.S. State Department, more than 200 business representatives will join the delegation.

item.title: The switch to the Latin script: the 1993 alphabet reform and its stages
item.description: After independence Uzbekistan, on 2 September 1993, adopted a law introducing a Latin-based Uzbek alphabet. This historical explainer sets out the succession of Arabic, Latin and Cyrillic scripts, the 1993 law, the 1995 revision and the three-decade-long transition — on the basis of sources, with precise dates and facts.

item.title: Uzbekistan ranks 71st and Kazakhstan 34th among the world's most powerful countries
item.description: World Population Review has published its 2026 list of the 100 most powerful countries. From Central Asia, only Kazakhstan (34) and Uzbekistan (71) made the list. The ranking is based on the perception-based U.S. News “Best Countries” study.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Water Resources Ministry rejects claims that the Amu Darya is drying up
item.description: The ministry cited hydropost data: on 9 October the water level at Termez was 27 cm higher than the same period in 2025; although discharge at Kerki fell by about 11%, the flow is being maintained. The decline was described as a seasonal process.

item.title: Uzbekistan presents its Center of Islamic Civilization at UNESCO
item.description: On 7 October at UNESCO headquarters in Paris, Uzbekistan put forward an international initiative to preserve Central Asia's scientific and spiritual heritage. More than 300 scholars and diplomats took part.

item.title: New Tashkent allocates 100 hectares to each region
item.description: On 12 October, in a dialogue with entrepreneurs, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced that each region and Tashkent district will receive 100 hectares. The same day, seven facilities worth $1 bln opened.

item.title: Uzbekistan has picked 3.4 mln tons of cotton — 76% of the plan
item.description: As of 12 October, about 75% of the harvest was done by machines. Last season, the labour inspectorate recovered 1.785 bln soums in unpaid wages for cotton pickers.

item.title: Uzbekistan strongly condemns the attack on Riyadh airport
item.description: On 10 October, Yemen's Houthis struck King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, the Saudi capital, with a ballistic missile: 12 people were killed and nearly 310 injured. Uzbekistan's Foreign Ministry called the attack a serious violation of international law.

item.title: Tashkent sets a green condition for greenhouses: filter or relocate
item.description: Greenhouses in and around Tashkent are being offered the chance to keep operating if they install filtered heating systems that meet standards. The reason: air pollution from coal heating.

item.title: Is the Amu Darya drying up? The Water Ministry rejects the claims
item.description: The ministry rejected social-media claims, saying that on 9 October the level at the Termez station was 27 cm higher than a year earlier and that the decline is seasonal.

item.title: The 1916 Turkestan revolt and the "mardikor" conscription: forced mobilisation, repression and mass flight
item.description: On 25 June 1916 (Old Style), Emperor Nicholas II of Russia issued a decree forcibly mobilising the native population of Turkestan and the Steppe region for rear-line labour in World War I (the "mardikor" call-up). It sparked Turkestan's largest anti-colonial revolt; the Jizzakh uprising was brutally suppressed, thousands died, and a mass flight began. This is a sourced historical explainer only.

item.title: The referendum of 26 March 1995: Islam Karimov's presidential term extended to 2000
item.description: On 26 March 1995 a referendum was held in Uzbekistan that extended President Islam Karimov's term — to which he had been elected in 1991 — until 2000, postponing the next presidential election. According to official results, 99.6% of those who voted said "yes." This is a sourced historical explainer only.

item.title: Islamic funeral and burial rites: how ghusl, kafan, the funeral prayer and burial are performed
item.description: In Islam, seeing off the deceased consists of four core acts: ghusl (washing), kafan (shrouding in white cloth), the funeral prayer (salat al-janazah), and burial (dafn). This explainer sets out each stage, the structure of the funeral prayer (four takbirs, with no bowing or prostration), the rules of mourning, and practical points for Uzbekistan and the diaspora abroad — on the basis of sources only. A religious rite is not a substitute for legal or personal advice.

item.title: What a deepfake is, and how to detect AI-generated fake video, audio and images
item.description: A deepfake is fake video, audio or imagery created or altered with artificial intelligence, making a real person appear to say something they never said or do something they never did. This explainer sets out how the technology works, real cases such as the 2024 US$25 million fraud, the practical signs for detecting synthetic content, and how to protect your family — on the basis of sources only.

item.title: Uzbekistan Airways to increase Kuala Lumpur flights to up to four a week
item.description: From late October the Tashkent–Kuala Lumpur frequency rises; S7 Airlines begins a codeshare on 25 October. Flights use the Boeing 787, and a 30-day visa-free regime applies for both countries' citizens.
